utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please announce the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-9-PT, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel. My name is Peter McCloskey, appearing for the first time on this case. I am joined by Gramsci di Fazio and Aisling Reidy for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Igor Pantelic, Defence counsel on behalf of my client, Dr. Blagoje Simic, who is today with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Miss Catherine Baen for Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Attorney Nowak Lukic from Belgrade for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and also assisting me, Mr. Krgovic, from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Borislav Pisarevic representing Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Pisarevic. Today's proceedings were originally designated as a Pre-Trial Conference. We'll have to change that to a Status Conference for the following reasons: We have two new Judges assigned to the case, Judges May and Fassi Fihri, and the Rules require the Chamber to examine the pre-trial briefs very closely, and this requires time for us to analyse the briefs and also for translation into both working languages. What we have decided to do, then, is to set the Pre-Trial Conference for Wednesday, the 27th of June, at 2.30 p.m. That would allow us to make the necessary preparations. I am to announce that the trial date for this case is set for the 10th of September, although it would be before a different composition of Judges, but the 10th of September. The accused persons who are now on provisional release are to return to the Detention Unit at least a week before the trial commences, and the Chamber will confirm this by an order nearer to that time. The sitting hours for the trial will be as requested to take account of Mr. Milan Simic's medical condition, four hours maximum per day. Mr. McCloskey, there are some matters relating to witnesses. I take it that you have been fully briefed. Facial distortion was granted for seven witnesses, and the OTP was to report as to whether a particular witness, Witness I, would testify with facial distortion or would seek closed session. That was by way of the order of the 26th May 1999, and the OTP indicated that it would check their position and report back. Are you in a position to tell us what the situation now is with Witness I?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will turn the floor over to Mr. di Fazio who has been, as you know, on this case. I have literally just been appointed to this case and have -- and I have all the confidence that Mr. di Fazio, as an experienced lawyer, will be able to deal with most of those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. The situation is that it's a non-issue. He's not on the witness list. We don't intend to call him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't intend to call Witness I? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see, okay. And the OTP was also to confirm, Mr. di Fazio, whether Todorovic's statements have been disclosed to Defence. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. The situation in that respect is this, if Your Honours please: Some interviews have been conducted. They -- the videos are available and are currently being transcribed and translated, and I expect that that entire task of, which relates to four - will Your Honours just bear with me - which relates to four interviews will be complete within four weeks and almost certainly sooner than that, but four weeks at the outside. So all of that material can be handed over easily within that time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Within four weeks? MR. DI FAZIO: Within four weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. di Fazio. There is a motion to amend the indictment. The motion is relatively simple. It seeks to remove Mr. Todorovic from the indictment; in respect of Blagoje Simic, it deletes the Article 7(3) responsibility charge; and in respect of Milan Simic, it deletes four counts, leaving the indictment with nine counts. The Chamber grants the motion, and a written decision to that effect will be issued shortly. Are there any other matters which counsel may wish to raise before I call on Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just for sake of clarification, it seems to me that on the last hearing regarding the -- Mr. Todorovic sentence, the learned colleague from the OTP bench Ms. Paterson stated that, in total, five interviews were conducted with Mr. Todorovic, so I would like to check whether it's five or four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I haven't been engaged in the task of transcribing and examining the interviews as yet. I intend to look at them in the very near future. My understanding is that there are only four interviews conducted thus far. It's likely a further interview will be conducted. That wasn't occurred yet. So at the moment, the task of transcribing and translating and redacting is ongoing, and that relates to only four interviews so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I hope that should clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Another issue, Your Honours. With your leave, I would formulate the application or motion regarding the, regarding the witnesses with pseudonyms because, as I am informed, in some other cases it was discovered -- I mean, the Defence was entitled to know the general, general facts or, I mean, names, et cetera, of course, subject to protective measures, in order to prepare the cross-examination, in order to prepare Defence. I mean, so if we are dealing with some witnesses with this kind of thing, I kindly and respectfully would like to formulate my motion. So subject to certain restrictions, of course, which are familiar with all of us, I apply for this ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, at the last Status Conference, I am reminded that the Prosecutor undertook to make that disclosure 30 days prior to the witness giving evidence, and at that time the Chamber felt that that was reasonable. On further thought, we believe that a period of six weeks would be more reasonable in the circumstances. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, if Your Honours -- yes, if Your Honours please, I can see no reason why that shouldn't be changed from 30 to 6 weeks, so I have no particular objection to that, but I can't say that I've examined the issue in detail. I've seen it in the transcript of the Status Conferences, and I would like to reserve the Prosecution's position, if I could, on that -- the Prosecution's response, if I could, on that issue. As I said, at this stage I can't see any obvious reason that stands out as to why the Prosecution should object to that; however, I do need some time to consider the reasons as to why that, that application was made, the reasons why that ruling was sought by the Prosecution. I can't address you on that at the moment, so that is the position. I could easily notify the Tribunal and my learned friends of the Prosecution's attitude on that aspect in a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, we'll give you 14 days -- MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- in which to make the response. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would an oral response to the Court's officer be sufficient, or do you expect a written response?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think in the circumstances a written response, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any other matters? Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to propose that the OTP be ordered in regard of production of transcripts of Mr. Stevan Todorovic, that the OTP be given a specific deadline, that is, a date for the production of these transcripts; and I propose that it be 20 June, seven days before the Pre-Trial Conference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will consult on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, how do you respond to that? MR. DI FAZIO: I have no problem --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise, Your Honours. I've got no problem with that, and I'm sure we can get the material to the Defence easily within that time. The only matter that arises is the possibility of a further interview, so I would ask that any order does not encompass or refer to a further interview, material obtained from Mr. Todorovic in a further interview; in other words, one that has not yet been conducted. Other than that, I'm sure that timetable can be adhered to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, then. The Chamber will require the OTP to make available to the Defence by the 20th of June transcripts of the four available interviews, and the additional interview or any other interview which is being conducted as quickly thereafter as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, will you stand. I have to ask you whether you have any matters that you wish to raise relating to the case or, in particular, to the conditions of your detention. THE ACCUSED B. SIMIC: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we are adjourned until the 27th of June at 2.30 p.m. Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there's just another matter or two that I would like to raise with the Tribunal, if I may -- the Chamber at this stage, if I may; that is, the question of further evidence. I intend to obtain some further evidence in the form of transcripts and statements relating to international armed conflict, so I'd like to put the Defence on notice of that, and that will invoke the use of Rule 92 bis, I believe. And secondly, I wondered if the Tribunal had in mind any period of time for this particular trial, or whether that is a matter to be decided at the Pre-Trial Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we will discuss that at the Pre-Trial Conference. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. In that case, I have no further issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are adjourned until Wednesday, 27th June, at 2.30 p.m.
